reading.title: The School Trip
reading.text: Last Friday our class went on a trip to a historic fort outside the city. It was only a day trip, but we left at seven in the morning. The trip took two hours by bus. Our teacher had planned it for weeks, and she gave us small maps and questions to answer. At the fort, a guide told us stories about the old soldiers. After lunch we played games in the park. On the trip home, most of us fell asleep. Everyone agreed that it was the best school trip of the year.

listening.script: Lena: Shall we plan a trip for the spring holidays? Tom: Good idea. A camping trip would be nice. Lena: I would prefer a boat trip on the river. Tom: Hmm. Camping is cheaper, and we can go for three days. Lena: OK, but let's check the weather first. If it rains, we will cancel the trip and go to the cinema instead. Tom: Agreed. I will ask Sam if he wants to come too.

reading.title: A Night Flight
reading.text: Amina booked a flight to London for her summer course. It was a long-haul flight, but a direct one, so she did not need to change planes. She arrived at the airport early because she did not want to miss her flight. The plane took off at ten in the evening. A friendly flight attendant brought her an in-flight meal and a blanket. Amina slept for a few hours and woke up when the pilot said the flight would land in thirty minutes. She was excited to see the city lights below.

reading.title: Delayed
reading.text: Our flight to Antalya was delayed by three hours. The airline apologised for the delay and gave every passenger a voucher for food. Heavy rain had caused delays to many flights that morning. While we waited, my brother and I read magazines and played cards. Finally the speaker said our plane was ready. Antalya is a popular holiday destination, and the plane was full of families. We reached our destination late in the evening, but the warm air and the smell of the sea made us forget the long wait.

reading.title: On the Ferry
reading.text: Every morning a small ferry carries passengers across the river. It can take about sixty people, and most of them are workers or students. When the ferry arrives, passengers board slowly, and a man checks their tickets. There is a passenger list for large groups, but ordinary travellers just pay at the gate. Last week a fellow passenger lost his hat in the wind, and the captain turned the boat back to find it. The man was very thankful. Now the other passengers say this is the friendliest ferry in town.

reading.title: Papers for the Journey
reading.text: Before her trip to Japan, Malika had to organise her documents. First, she checked that her passport was valid, because it would expire soon. She decided to renew it and had a new passport photo taken. Then she went online to apply for a tourist visa. The visa application took ten minutes to fill in, and she waited two weeks for the answer. At the airport, an officer at passport control looked at her passport and the visa and smiled. Malika said that the hardest part of travelling is not the flight, but the paperwork.

reading.title: Travelling Light
reading.text: Jasur is going to visit his aunt in another city. He has packed light luggage because he only needs clothes for two days. He keeps his carry-on luggage on the seat next to him, so he can get it quickly. The train fare is not expensive, but he bought a return ticket so he does not need to pay again. Last year his friend lost his luggage at a station, and the whole trip became difficult. Now Jasur always writes his name and phone number on his bag. He also checks his tickets twice before he leaves home.
